query: What factors explain low review scores?

per_column.name: is_low_score
per_column.rationale: Binary encoding of the focus variable; the outcome itself, restated from the query.

per_column.name: helpfulness_ratio
per_column.rationale: Helpfulness votes are plausibly caused by review content/score reception rather than causing the score; adjusting for it risks collider bias, not a common cause of the review-writing behavior and the score.

per_column.name: review_length
per_column.rationale: A generic text-length feature. It is a property of the review text, correlated with score but not a plausible upstream common cause; closer to a descriptor/proxy than a confounder.

per_column.name: word_count
per_column.rationale: Mechanical token count; generic, does not represent a common cause of a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: has_exclamation
per_column.rationale: Stylistic text feature; a downstream expression of the reviewer's sentiment rather than a common cause; not a confounder.

per_column.name: has_question
per_column.rationale: Stylistic text feature, generic; not a common cause of a treatment and the outcome.

per_column.name: negative_word_count
per_column.rationale: Negative language expresses the reviewer's (dis)satisfaction; it lies on the path between an experience and the assigned score rather than being an upstream common cause. Treating it as a confounder would be an error.

per_column.name: positive_word_count
per_column.rationale: Same as negative_word_count: sentiment expressed in text is on the causal path to the score, a mediator/proxy of the outcome, not a confounder.

per_column.name: sentiment_ratio
per_column.rationale: Derived sentiment measure that essentially encodes the same satisfaction that drives the score; mediator/near-outcome, not a common cause.

per_column.name: summary_length
per_column.rationale: Generic length feature of the summary text; not a plausible common cause of treatment and outcome.

per_column.name: caps_ratio
per_column.rationale: Stylistic emphasis feature; downstream expression of reviewer emotion, not an upstream common cause.

per_column.name: product_avg_score
per_column.rationale: Underlying product quality plausibly causes both how a given reviewer tends to rate (treatment behavior) and the individual low score outcome; a genuine common cause surfaced from data.

per_column.name: user_avg_score
per_column.rationale: Reviewer's baseline harshness/leniency causes both their propensity to be a harsh reviewer (treatment) and the low score outcome; a genuine common cause surfaced from data.

per_column.name: score_vs_product_avg
per_column.rationale: Computed as a function of the score itself relative to product average; it is derived from the outcome and thus a collider/near-outcome, not a valid confounder.

per_column.name: reviewer_is_harsh
per_column.rationale: A binary indicator of reviewer harshness serves as the candidate cause (treatment) whose effect on the low score is being attributed.

judge.rationale: A plausible treatment (reviewer_is_harsh) is present, and the query names no confounders, so any valid common cause counts toward the capability. product_avg_score is a genuine common cause (product quality drives both rating tendency and the low score) surfaced from data. user_avg_score partly overlaps with the harshness treatment (near-definitional to reviewer_is_harsh, which is derived from user_avg_score), weakening it as an independent confounder. The bulk of added columns are generic text/style features, sentiment mediators expressing the same satisfaction that produces the score, or outcome-derived colliders (helpfulness_ratio, score_vs_product_avg). Because the strongest 'confounders' are mixed with a mediated/collider-heavy set and one confounder is effectively the treatment's own definition, the confounder_quality is only moderate.
